payload.text: `intent llm` renders the agent guide from the dispatch table; no hand-maintained command list exists --- **THE TWO CLAUSES HAVE DIFFERENT SCOPES AND THE ROW NEVER SAID SO. RULED BY vc 2026-08-30 ON ic's ASK, AGAINST THE READING THAT WOULD HAVE CLOSED IT.** Clause 1 is GUIDE-SCOPED and is now genuinely asserted; clause 2 is ESTATE-SCOPED and is not. **THE ARGUMENT IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE: a guide that renders from the table keeps no list of its own BY DEFINITION, so a guide-scoped clause 2 would restate clause 1** -- and a reading that makes half a row redundant is the wrong reading. Clause 2 is doing different work or it is doing none. **CLAUSE 1 IS CLOSED AND IT WAS NOT BEFORE `7ecb1e62`, WHICH IS ic's FINDING AND THE BETTER HALF OF THIS ENTRY.** Every test in `guide.rs` drove the COMMITTED table, so all of them passed equally against a guide that DERIVES its list and one that keeps its own and happens to MATCH. **Agreement is not derivation, and the difference is invisible on every tree where the two coincide** -- which is every tree until someone adds a row. Proved by mutation: point `command_reference` at the compiled-in table rather than the one it was passed, and 13 pass while 1 fails. **Until that commit the guide could have stopped deriving from the table entirely and the whole file stayed green.** **CLAUSE 2's SUBJECT IS `render.rs`'s `SERVED_BY_DAEMON`** -- a hand-kept list of command PATHS, `const` in Rust, whose `"st list"` string nothing checks against the table. Driven by vc: it appears in `render.rs` and nowhere else, so a renamed or retired path leaves it silently stale. **The population is ONE, measured rather than assumed, which is what makes the estate reading affordable** -- a sweep of every path-keyed `const` in both crates finds column headers, status enums, formats and probe frames, and exactly one roster of command paths. **THE CHECK IS ic's OWN SHAPE AND IT IS THE RIGHT ONE: every hand-kept roster of command paths is either DERIVED from the table or DECLARED as an exception WITH A DISCHARGE CONDITION.** `SERVED_BY_DAEMON` gets a real one -- it discharges when the daemon serves the surface -- so it becomes a declared exception rather than an unnoticed second home. **That is `EXPECTED_DISAGREEMENTS`' shape used correctly**, the roster whose `help` entry was deleted the same day for naming its own discharge condition and having it met. **THE CHECK IS WP-09's AND THE SUBJECT IS WP-08's CODE, WHICH IS FINE AND WORTH STATING** so neither node reads the other's ownership as a blocker.
